name: Atacama — Yungay
description: One of the driest places on Earth. Some spots go years without rain, and the soil holds almost no life, a lot like Mars.
access: Paved road from Antofagasta (~1.5 h); ANF airport

name: Haughton Crater
description: A 23 km meteor crater in the Canadian Arctic. It is cold, dry and rocky, and NASA has tested rovers and spacesuits here for decades.
access: Twin Otter charter from Resolute Bay; no roads

name: Devon Island — FMARS plateau
description: A bare, frozen plateau beside Haughton Crater, home to the FMARS mock Mars base where crews lived like astronauts.
access: Twin Otter charter from Resolute Bay; summer only

name: Death Valley
description: A scorching desert basin with salt flats, dunes and old lakebeds. Rovers like Curiosity were tested here.
access: Paved CA-190; Las Vegas airport ~2 h

name: McMurdo Dry Valleys (Wright Valley)
description: Ice-free valleys in Antarctica, the coldest and driest desert on Earth. Frozen soil and fierce winds make it a classic Mars stand-in.
access: Helicopter from McMurdo Station; Antarctic Treaty permit

name: Mauna Kea
description: A huge volcano in Hawaiʻi. Its high, dusty slopes of volcanic ash look like lunar soil, and NASA has used them for Moon equipment tests.

name: Río Tinto
description: A river turned blood-red by iron and acid. Microbes thrive in water that would kill most life, which helps us imagine life on Mars.

name: Iceland highlands — Askja / Holuhraun
description: Black lava fields and sand in Iceland's empty interior. Apollo astronauts trained here before going to the Moon.

name: Lanzarote — Timanfaya
description: A volcanic island with fresh lava flows and lava tubes. ESA trains astronauts here to do geology on other worlds.

name: Utah — MDRS / Hanksville
description: Red, rocky badlands in Utah. Crews live inside the Mars Desert Research Station habitat and practise Mars missions.
access: Paved road from Hanksville; Grand Junction airport ~3 h

name: Kilbourne Hole
description: A wide volcanic crater in the New Mexico desert, used to train Apollo astronauts.
access: Dirt roads from Las Cruces / El Paso (~1 h)

name: Craters of the Moon
description: Huge lava fields and lava tube caves in Idaho, where NASA tests how astronauts might explore volcanic terrain.
access: US-20/26 paved; Idaho Falls airport ~1.5 h

name: Danakil Depression — Dallol
description: A boiling, acidic hot-spring field in one of the hottest places on Earth, full of yellow and green salt crusts. It shows the limits of life.
access: 4x4 from Mekele (~4 h); guided convoys only

name: Erta Ale
description: An active shield volcano with a lava lake, surrounded by fresh black basalt in the Afar desert.

name: Lut Desert — Kaluts / Gandom Beryan
description: A blistering desert of wind-carved ridges called yardangs. It has recorded some of the hottest ground temperatures on Earth.

name: Salar de Uyuni
description: The world's largest salt flat. It is flat, bright white and very high up, so it gets intense sunlight.

name: Altiplano — Laguna Verde / Licancabur
description: High Andes lakes beside a volcano at 4,300 m. Thin air, strong UV and salty water make it a test site for searching for life.

name: Namib — Sossusvlei
description: Towering red dunes and white clay pans in one of the world's oldest deserts. Life here survives mainly on fog.

name: Qaidam Basin — Dalangtan (Tibetan Plateau)
description: A high, dry basin on the Tibetan Plateau full of salt and wind-carved rocks, often called the most Mars-like place in China.

name: Changtang Plateau
description: A vast, cold, high-altitude plateau with frozen ground and salty lakes, and very few people.

name: Svalbard — Bockfjorden
description: Arctic volcanoes and hot springs on Svalbard, used to test Mars rover instruments.

name: Kamchatka — Tolbachik lava fields
description: Fresh lava fields and cinder cones in Kamchatka, where Soviet lunar rovers were tested.

name: El Pinacate
description: A volcanic desert with giant round craters in Mexico. Apollo astronauts trained here.
access: Hwy 8 Sonoyta–Puerto Peñasco; gravel in reserve

name: Tindouf hamada
description: A flat, stony desert plain in the Sahara, wind-swept and very dry.
access: Tindouf airport; border area, access restricted

name: Wadi Rum
description: Red sand and towering sandstone cliffs in Jordan, a popular film stand-in for Mars.

name: Lonar Crater
description: A meteor crater punched into volcanic basalt, one of the few on Earth, similar to craters on the Moon.

name: Meteor Crater
description: A crisp, 1.2 km wide meteor crater in Arizona where Apollo astronauts learned crater geology.

name: San Francisco Volcanic Field — SP Crater
description: A neat black cinder cone and lava flow north of Flagstaff, used for NASA field tests.

name: Undara lava tubes
description: Some of the longest lava tubes on Earth. These underground tunnels are like the caves that might shelter future Moon or Mars bases.

name: Kazumura Cave
description: The longest and deepest lava tube known on Earth, running for 65 km under Hawaiʻi.

name: Mojave — Amboy Crater
description: A young cinder cone and lava field in the Mojave Desert, easy to reach by road.

name: Pilbara — Dresser Formation
description: Some of the oldest rocks on Earth, holding 3.5-billion-year-old signs of life. They help scientists recognise ancient life on Mars.
access: Gravel from Marble Bar; Port Hedland airport

name: Axel Heiberg — Gypsum Hill springs
description: Cold, salty springs that flow all year in the Arctic, a model for possible springs on Mars.
access: Charter from Resolute; McGill Arctic Research Station

name: Union Glacier blue-ice field
description: Wind-scoured blue ice in deep Antarctica, cold and lifeless, with a long polar day and night like the lunar poles.
access: Ilyushin flights from Punta Arenas; Antarctic Treaty permit

name: Gobi — Bayanzag (Flaming Cliffs)
description: Red cliffs and dusty plains in the Gobi Desert, famous for dinosaur fossils.

name: Sahara — Hoggar / Atakor volcanic field
description: Ancient volcanic peaks rising from the Sahara, rocky, dry and high.

name: Richat Structure
description: A giant 40 km bullseye of rock rings in the Sahara, visible from space.
access: Gravel tracks from Ouadane; Atar airport

name: Painted Desert — Blue Mesa
description: Blue and purple clay hills in Arizona's Painted Desert. These clays are like the ones rovers search for on Mars.
access: I-40; Petrified Forest NP park road

name: Mono Lake tufa
description: A salty lake with strange limestone towers called tufa. Its mineral-rich water is a model for ancient Martian lakes.

name: Lake Salda
description: A turquoise lake whose white shore minerals match those seen from orbit in Jezero Crater. It helped plan the Perseverance mission.
access: Paved road from Burdur; Denizli airport

name: Black Point Lava Flow
description: A basalt lava flow north of Flagstaff where NASA ran its Desert RATS rover and spacewalk field tests, most recently in 2022.
access: Dirt roads from US-89, ~1 h from Flagstaff
